title: Misattributed sub-second batch accounting causing billing deltas for multi-tenant deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private reported unexplained billing increases and negative token deltas on hourly reports. Support cases indicate tokens were sometimes attributed to the wrong tenant or to a shared system account during short, high-throughput bursts. This ticket scopes investigation, a short-term mitigation, and a code fix to correct accounting and prevent recurrence.
root_cause_summary: A race condition in the per-batch attribution code path surfaced when continuous batching and the shared aggregation worker were enabled. During KV-cache hits and model fallback, request metadata (tenant_id) could be overwritten before per-token deltas were flushed, leading to tokens being recorded under the wrong account or the system service account. The aggregator also merged partial window deltas using a map keyed by request timestamp truncated to the second, which collided for rapid micro-batches.
mitigations_taken:
- Deployed a config toggle to disable cross-request pooling for affected customers within 30 minutes of triage.
- Paused automatic model fallback for dedicated pools in the affected regions as interim step.
- Issued customer notifications and opened credit remediation for impacted billing cycles.
proposed_fix: 1) Add immutable request-level attribution object copied at batch enqueue time to avoid metadata races. 2) Replace timestamp-second-indexed aggregator with monotonic batch sequence IDs. 3) Add defensive checks in the reconciler to detect and reject negative deltas. 4) Add unit/integration tests that simulate sub-second micro-batching under high KV cache hit rates.
rollback_plan: If the runtime change causes regressions, revert the aggregator change and re-enable the config toggle that disables cross-request pooling for the short term. Billing credits will be applied manually for the rollback window while we stabilize.
verification_plan:
- End-to-end test in staging with synthetic multi-tenant load reproducing the race.
- Run reconciliation job comparing per-tenant token sums pre/post fix for a 24h window.
- Canary deploy to 10% of Hosted traffic then to Dedicated pools with smoke checks (token parity, latency, error rates).
- Contact top-5 impacted customers to verify their billing reports.
comments: 2025-02-18: Triage call — Aisha, Daniel, Priya (SRE) and Marco (billing) present. Immediate mitigation: disable cross-request pooling for affected dedicated pools. Notified customers and opened credits.

2025-02-19: Reproduced root cause in local harness by simulating KV cache hits and model fallback; observed tenant_id mutation at Batch.enqueue() -> assigned to Daniel to prototype immutable attribution object.

2025-02-21: Staging deploy passed smoke tests; reconciliation job shows reduced misattribution but 0.03% residual variance; extended logging for aggregator windows.
2025-02-24: Canary deploy to 10% Hosted traffic underway; monitoring dashboards show token parity within threshold. Plan to expand canary tomorrow if no regressions.
